stories.title: Serena + Venus Williams Fall in Emotional Doubles Debut

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text: Serena & Venus lost their Cincinnati doubles debut 2-6, 6-1, 10-8 to Kostyuk/Stearns. Led 9-8 in the match tiebreak — Venus double fault ended it. First doubles match together since 2022 US Open. Heartbreak. #Tennis #Cincinnati #Serena #Venus

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text: They came so close. Serena (44) and Venus (46) led the match tiebreak 9-8 before a double fault on match point ended their Cincinnati run. Two legends, one last dance. #Tennis #WilliamsSisters #Cincinnati #WTA

facebook.long_form:
Window: 8:00 AM ET

They came within a double fault of something magical.

Serena (44) and Venus Williams (46) made their emotional return to doubles tennis together Monday night in Cincinnati — their first pairing since the 2022 US Open — and gave the crowd everything they could have asked for before falling 2-6, 6-1, 10-8 to Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns.

The first set wasn't close. But the sisters came to life in the second, racing through it 6-1, and suddenly you could feel the energy shift inside Lindner Family Tennis Centre. The match tiebreak had everything — and when Venus and Serena clawed back to 9-8, you started to wonder. Then a double fault on match point from Venus, and it was over.

There's no shame in that exit. Two legends, 90 combined years of life experience, playing at one of the biggest events on the hard-court swing. The reception they received says everything about what they mean to this sport.

What's your favourite Williams sisters doubles memory?

article.headline: Serena and Venus Williams Fall in Emotional Cincinnati Doubles Debut

stories.title: Swiatek Storms Back From Set Down to Beat Sakkari

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text: Iga Swiatek lost the first set but won 12 of the last 14 games to beat Sakkari 4-6, 6-1, 6-1 in Cincinnati R3. Eight-match winning streak. Defending champion into the last 16. #Tennis #Swiatek #Cincinnati #WTA

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text: Down a set to Sakkari, Swiatek locked in and didn't look back. 4-6, 6-1, 6-1. Her 2026 form heading into the US Open is as sharp as it gets. #Swiatek #Cincinnati #USOpen #WTA

facebook.long_form:
Window: 10:30 AM ET

Iga Swiatek has been here before. Down a set, the crowd sensing an upset — and then she just turns it on.

Maria Sakkari won the first set 6-4 Monday in Cincinnati and looked sharp doing it. But from that point on, Swiatek was relentless. She won 12 of the last 14 games, taking the second and third sets 6-1, 6-1 to advance to the Round of 16.

That's eight consecutive wins. She's the defending Cincinnati champion. The US Open is 12 days away. And she's playing some of the best tennis of her season right now — which, given her résumé, is saying something.

Sakkari gave her a real test in that first set. Swiatek's answer was emphatic.

Who do you think emerges from the WTA side of the draw at the US Open?

article.headline: Swiatek Drops First Set, Then Dominates Sakkari to Reach Cincinnati Last 16

stories.title: Jodar Drops Just 3 Games to Crush Tabilo in 75 Minutes

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text: Rafael Jodar dropped just 3 games to Tabilo (6-2, 6-1) and is in the Cincinnati R4. He joins Alcaraz and Shelton as the only teenagers to reach this stage in Cincinnati this decade. 19 years old. The future is now. #Tennis #Jodar #NextGenATP #Cincinnati

facebook.long_form:
Window: 10:30 AM ET

Rafael Jodar is 19 years old and he just dropped three games in a Cincinnati Masters 1000 match.

The Spanish teenager dismantled Alejandro Tabilo 6-2, 6-1 in 75 minutes Monday, smashing 26 winners to reach the Round of 16. Only Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton have done the same as teenagers in Cincinnati this decade — Jodar now joins that list.

He started 2026 ranked No. 168. Now he's in the Cincinnati last 16 in August with the US Open less than two weeks away. When was the last time you watched a 19-year-old play like this on a big stage?

article.headline: Jodar Drops Just 3 Games to Crush Tabilo, Joins Alcaraz and Shelton in Elite Cincinnati Teen Club

stories.title: Zverev and Rybakina Grind Through to R4

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text: Zverev survives two tiebreaks to beat Atmane 7-6, 7-6 (his 46th win of 2026). Rybakina beats Frech 6-4, 7-6 through two rain delays. Both top seeds into the Cincinnati R4. #Tennis #Zverev #Rybakina #Cincinnati

facebook.long_form:
Window: 12:30 PM ET

The top seeds took care of business, but they didn't have it easy.

Alexander Zverev (No. 1 seed) needed every point in both tiebreaks to outlast Terrance Atmane 7-6(4), 7-6(6) on Monday in Cincinnati, picking up his 46th win of 2026. It was the kind of match you have to grind through — and Zverev did exactly that.

On the WTA side, Elena Rybakina (No. 2 seed) beat Magdalena Frech 6-4, 7-6(2) while enduring two rain stoppages. Rain delays can kill a player's rhythm. Rybakina played like the weather wasn't happening.

Both top seeds are through to Wednesday's Round of 16, where the brackets are getting serious fast.

Which match are you most looking forward to in the Cincinnati R4?

article.headline: Zverev Grinds Through Double Tiebreak, Rybakina Fights Rain to Set Up Cincinnati R4

stories.title: Anisimova Ends Eala's Run; US Open 12 Days Out

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text: Anisimova rallies past Eala 4-6, 6-4, 6-2 to reach the Cincinnati last 16 for the first time since 2018. US Open in 12 days — Sinner and Alcaraz both on the entry list but neither has played a match in weeks. #Tennis #Cincinnati #USOpen #ATP

facebook.long_form:
Window: 6:00 PM ET

Alex Eala's 2026 hard-court season will be remembered. It just didn't end the way she wanted.

The Filipina dropped the opening set 4-6 to No. 9 seed Amanda Anisimova on Monday in Cincinnati, won the next set 6-4, and then found herself on the wrong end of a 6-2 third set as Anisimova found another gear. It sends Eala home in R3 and puts Anisimova in the last 16 for the first time in Cincinnati since 2018.

Meanwhile, the US Open draw looms. August 27 is when we find out who plays who in New York. And the biggest question hanging over both draws: will Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz be 100%? Sinner hasn't played since Wimbledon. Alcaraz hasn't played a competitive match since April. Both are on the entry list. Neither is confirmed healthy.

Twelve days. Tick tock.

Who do you think wins the 2026 US Open?

article.headline: Anisimova Ends Eala's Cincinnati Run; US Open Looms 12 Days Away
